title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 92 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 496–500 (Night 92, continuing directly from nights-91), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 92 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. A masked young horseman routs the Christians and is revealed to Sharrukān as his brother, King Ḍawʾ al-Makān; the vizier Dandān and the emir Bahrām spring the ambush from the shore, and the Rūm are slaughtered and their fleet taken, all but twenty ships. In Constantinople the victory celebrations turn to mourning, the patriarch blames some hidden sin, and the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī disguises herself as a Muslim ascetic and sets out with a hundred Christians of the Syrian Najrān to destroy the Muslim commander by guile. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ وَالتِّسْعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thāniyatu wa-al-tisʿūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the second-and-ninetieth,
sentences.i: And when it was the ninety-second night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الْكُفَّارَ صَاحُوا عَلَى بَعْضِهِمْ قَائِلِينَ خُذُوا بِثَأْرِ لُوقَا
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-kuffāra ṣāḥū ʿalā baʿḍihim qāʾilīna khudhū bi-thaʾri lūqā
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the unbelievers cried out upon one another, saying: Take the vengeance of Lūqā!
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the unbelievers shouted to one another, “Avenge Lūqā!”
sentences.n: The night opens by repeating the last words of the one before. خذ بثأر, “take up the blood-debt of”, with bi- marking the one avenged.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ مَلِكُ الرُّومِ يُنَادِي يَا لَأَخْذِ ثَأْرِ أَبْرِيزَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra maliku al-rūmi yunādī yā la-akhdhi thaʾri abrīzata
sentences.l: And the king of the Rūm began calling: O for the taking of the vengeance of Abrīza!
sentences.i: and the king of the Rūm kept crying out, “Vengeance for Abrīza!”
sentences.n: Yā la- with the genitive is the cry of summons: “O for …!”. Abrīza is the king's daughter, killed earlier in the tale.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ صَاحَ الْمَلِكُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَقَالَ يَا عِبَادَ الْمَلِكِ الدَّيَّانِ اضْرِبُوا أَهْلَ الْكُفْرِ وَالطُّغْيَانِ بِبِيضِ الصِّفَاحِ وَسُمْرِ الرِّمَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika ṣāḥa al-maliku ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-qāla yā ʿibāda al-maliki al-dayyāni iḍribū ahla al-kufri wa-al-ṭughyāni bi-bīḍi al-ṣifāḥi wa-sumri al-rimāḥi
sentences.l: And at that the king Ḍawʾ al-Makān cried out and said: O servants of the King, the Judge, strike the people of unbelief and of tyranny with the white of the broad-blades and the brown of the lances!
sentences.i: At that King Ḍawʾ al-Makān shouted, “Servants of the King who judges all, strike the people of unbelief and tyranny with flashing white blades and tawny lances!”
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-dayyān / al-ṭughyān, al-ṣifāḥ / al-rimāḥ. “The King, the Judge” (al-malik al-dayyān) is God. Bi-bīḍ: bi- “with”, the instrument.

sentences.t: فَرَجَعَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ وَأَعْمَلُوا فِيهِمُ الصَّارِمَ الْبَتَّارَ
sentences.tr: fa-rajaʿa al-muslimūna ʿalā al-kuffāri wa-aʿmalū fīhimu al-ṣārima al-battāra
sentences.l: And the Muslims turned back upon the unbelievers and set to work in them the sharp, the severing (sword).
sentences.i: The Muslims turned back on the unbelievers and plied the keen, cleaving sword among them.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ يُنَادِي مُنَادِى الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَيَقُولُ عَلَيْكُمْ بِأَعْدَاءِ الدِّينِ يَا مُحِبَّ النَّبِىِّ الْمُخْتَارِ هَذَا وَقْتُ إِرْضَاءِ الْكَرِيمِ الْغَفَّارِ يَارَاجِيَ النَّجَاةِ فِى الْيَوْمِ الْمَخُوفِ إِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ تَحْتَ ظِلَالِ السُّيُوفِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra yunādī munādī al-muslimīna wa-yaqūlu ʿalaykum bi-aʿdāʾi al-dīni yā muḥibba al-nabiyyi al-mukhtāri hādhā waqtu irḍāʾi al-karīmi al-ghaffāri yā rājiya al-najāti fī al-yawmi al-makhūfi inna al-jannata taḥta ẓilāli al-suyūfi
sentences.l: And the crier of the Muslims began calling and saying: Upon you the enemies of the religion! O lover of the Prophet, the chosen one, this is the time of pleasing the Generous, the Forgiving! O hoper of salvation on the day feared, Paradise is beneath the shades of the swords!
sentences.i: and the Muslims' herald went about crying, “At the enemies of the faith! You who love the chosen Prophet, now is the time to please the Generous, the All-Forgiving! You who hope to be saved on the day of terror, Paradise lies beneath the shade of swords!”
sentences.n: The print has باراجي, a misprint for يا راجي (“O you who hope”), corrected here; the two words stay run together as printed. عليكم بـ, “upon you with”, means “go for, take hold of”. The herald's cry rhymes: al-mukhtār / al-ghaffār, al-makhūf / al-suyūf; “Paradise is beneath the shade of swords” is a saying ascribed to the Prophet.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِشَرْكَانَ قَدْ حَمَلَ هُوَ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ وَقَطَعُوا عَلَيْهِمْ طَرِيقَ الْفِرَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-sharrukāna qad ḥamala huwa wa-man maʿahu ʿalā al-kuffāri wa-qaṭaʿū ʿalayhim ṭarīqa al-firāri
sentences.l: And behold, Sharrukān had charged, he and whoever was with him, upon the unbelievers, and they cut upon them the road of flight.
sentences.i: And now Sharrukān charged the unbelievers with all his men, and they cut off their way of escape.
sentences.n: Wa-idhā bi- marks what comes suddenly into view: the bi- only introduces it, “and behold, Sharrukān …”.

sentences.t: وَجَالَ بَيْنَ الصُّفُوفِ وَطَافَ وَإِذَا بِفَارِسٍ مَلِيحِ الِانْعِطَافِ قَدْ فَتَحَ فِي عَسْكَرِ الْكُفَّارِ مَيْدَانًا وَجَالَ فِي الْكَفَرَةِ حَرْبًا وَطِعَانًا وَمَلَأَ الْأَرْضَ رُؤُسًا وَأَبْدَانًا
sentences.tr: wa-jāla bayna al-ṣufūfi wa-ṭāfa wa-idhā bi-fārisin malīḥi al-inʿiṭāfi qad fataḥa fī ʿaskari al-kuffāri maydānan wa-jāla fī al-kafarati ḥarban wa-ṭiʿānan wa-malaʾa al-arḍa ruʾūsan wa-abdānan
sentences.l: And he roamed between the ranks and circled; and behold, a horseman, comely of bending, had opened in the army of the unbelievers a field, and roamed among the unbelievers in war and lance-thrusting, and filled the earth with heads and bodies.
sentences.i: He wheeled up and down between the ranks; and behold, a graceful, supple horseman had cleared himself a field in the unbelievers' army and was ranging among them, fighting and thrusting, strewing the ground with heads and bodies.
sentences.n: The one who wheels between the ranks is Sharrukān; the horseman is not yet named. Rhymed: ṭāf / al-inʿiṭāf, maydānan / ṭiʿānan / abdānan.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ خَافَتِ الْكُفَّارُ مِنْ حَرْبِهِ وَمَالَتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لِطَعْنِهِ وَضَرْبِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad khāfati al-kuffāru min ḥarbihi wa-mālat aʿnāquhum li-ṭaʿnihi wa-ḍarbihi
sentences.l: And the unbelievers had feared his war, and their necks had bent to his thrusting and his striking.
sentences.i: The unbelievers dreaded his onslaught and bowed their necks to his thrusts and blows.
sentences.n: The print has ومانت, a misprint for ومالت (“and bent”), corrected here. خافت الكفار: a feminine verb with a broken plural, as often.

sentences.t: قَدْ تَقَلَّدَ بِسَيْفَيْنِ لَحْظٍ وَحُسَامٍ وَاعْتَقَلَ بِرُمْحَيْنِ قَنَاةٍ وَقَوَامٍ بِوَفْرَةٍ تُغْنِي عَنْ وَافِرِ عَدَدِ الْعَسَاكِرِ كَمَا قَالَ فِيهِ الشَّاعِرُ
sentences.tr: qad taqallada bi-sayfayni laḥẓin wa-ḥusāmin wa-iʿtaqala bi-rumḥayni qanātin wa-qawāmin bi-wafratin tughnī ʿan wāfiri ʿadadi al-ʿasākiri kamā qāla fīhi al-shāʿiru
sentences.l: He had girded himself with two swords, a glance and a blade, and couched two lances, a shaft and a stature, with a lock of hair that makes needless the abundant number of the armies, as the poet said of him:
sentences.i: He had girt on two swords, his glance and his blade, and couched two lances, his spear-shaft and his slender stature, and wore a mane of hair worth a whole host of soldiers; as the poet said of such a one:
sentences.n: The conceit is a love-poet's: the youth's glance is a sword and his straight figure a lance. Wafra is a full head of hair falling to the ear-lobes, and it plays on wāfir, “abundant”.

sentences.t:
لَا تَحْسُنُ الْوَفْرَةُ اِلَّا وَهِيْ * مَنْشُورَةُ الْفَرْعَيْنِ يَوْمَ النِّزَالِ
عَلَى فَتًى مُعْتَقِلٍ صَعْدَةً * يُعِلُّهَا مِنْ كُلِّ وَافِى السِّبَالِ
sentences.tr:
lā taḥsunu al-wafratu illā wa-hiya * manshūratu al-farʿayni yawma al-nizāli
ʿalā fatan muʿtaqilin ṣaʿdatan * yuʿilluhā min kulli wāfī al-sibāli
sentences.l:
Not fair is the lock of hair except while it is * spread out in its two branches on the day of combat,
upon a youth couching a straight lance, * giving it a second draught from every full-moustached one.
sentences.i:
A mane of hair is never fair but when it streams * unbound in both its locks upon the day of war
above a youth who couches a straight spear * and gives it drink again from every bearded foe.
sentences.n: Verse, as printed with its own pointing. Yuʿilluhā: he gives the lance its second draught (ʿalal) — of blood, from every grown warrior with full moustaches.

sentences.t: وَيَقُولُ الْآخَرُ
sentences.tr: wa-yaqūlu al-ākharu
sentences.l: And the other says:
sentences.i: And another says:

sentences.t:
اَقُوْلُ لَهُ لَمَّا تَقَلَّدَ سَيْفَهُ * كَفَتْكَ سُيُوفُ اللَّحْظِ عَنْ ذَلِكَ الْعَضْبِ
فَقَالَ لِحَاظِيْ سَيْفُهَا لِذَوِى الْهَوَى * وَسَيْفِيْ لِمَنْ لَمْ يَدْرِ مَالَذَّةُ الْحُبِّ
sentences.tr:
aqūlu lahu lammā taqallada sayfahu * kafatka suyūfu al-laḥẓi ʿan dhālika al-ʿaḍbi
fa-qāla liḥāẓī sayfuhā li-dhawī al-hawā * wa-sayfī li-man lam yadri mā ladhdhatu al-ḥubbi
sentences.l:
I say to him when he girded on his sword: * The swords of the glance have sufficed you instead of that sharp blade.
And he said: My glances — their sword is for those of passion, * and my sword is for whoever knows not what the pleasure of love is.
sentences.i:
When he girt on his sword I said to him, * “The swords of your glance are enough without that blade.”
He said, “My glances' sword is for the ones who love; * my sword's for him who never knew love's sweetness.”
sentences.n: The print has اْعَضْبِ, a misprint for الْعَضْبِ (“the sharp blade”) with the lām dropped, corrected here. Otherwise the verse is as printed, with its own pointing; مالذة runs mā, “what”, and ladhdha, “pleasure”, together.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهُ شَرْكَانُ قَالَ أُعِيذُكَ بِالْقُرْآنِ وَآيَاتِ الرَّحْمَنِ مَنْ أَنْتَ أَيُّهَا الْفَارِسُ مِنَ الْفُرْسَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhu sharrukānu qāla uʿīdhuka bi-al-qurʾāni wa-āyāti al-raḥmāni man anta ayyuhā al-fārisu mina al-fursāni
sentences.l: And when Sharrukān saw him he said: I commend you for refuge to the Qurʾān and the verses of the Merciful — who are you, O horseman of the horsemen?
sentences.i: When Sharrukān saw him he said, “I commend you to the protection of the Qurʾān and the verses of the Merciful! Who are you, horseman among horsemen?
sentences.n: أعيذك بـ, “I place you in the refuge of”, wards off the evil eye from someone admired; bi- names the protector.

sentences.t: فَلَقَدْ أَرْضَيْتَ بِفِعْلِكَ الْمَلِكَ الدَّيَّانَ الَّذِى لَايَشْغَلُهُ شَأْنٌ عَنْ شَأْنٍ حَيْثُ هَزَمْتَ أَهْلَ الْكُفْرِ وَالطُّغْيَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-la-qad arḍayta bi-fiʿlika al-malika al-dayyāna alladhī lā yashghaluhu shaʾnun ʿan shaʾnin ḥaythu hazamta ahla al-kufri wa-al-ṭughyāni
sentences.l: For indeed you have pleased by your deed the King, the Judge, whom no affair distracts from an affair, inasmuch as you have routed the people of unbelief and of tyranny.
sentences.i: By what you have done you have pleased the King and Judge, whom no one matter turns from another, for you have routed the people of unbelief and tyranny.”
sentences.n: “Whom no matter distracts from another” is a stock phrase for God, who attends to everything at once. The print runs لا and يشغله together.

sentences.t: فَنَادَاهُ الْفَارِسُ قَائِلًا أَنْتَ الَّذِي بِالْأَمْسِ عَاهَدْتَنِي فَمَا أَسْرَعَ مَانَسِيتَنِي
sentences.tr: fa-nādāhu al-fārisu qāʾilan anta alladhī bi-al-amsi ʿāhadtanī fa-mā asraʿa mā nasītanī
sentences.l: And the horseman called to him, saying: You are the one who yesterday made a covenant with me — so how quick that you have forgotten me!
sentences.i: The horseman called back, “You are the one who made a pact with me only yesterday — how quickly you have forgotten me!”
sentences.n: فما أسرع ما is the form of wonder: “how quick it was that …”. The print runs ما and نسيتني together. Bi-al-ams: bi- “at”, of time.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ كَشَفَ اللِّثَامَ عَنْ وَجْهِهِ حَتَّى ظَهَرَ مَاخَفِيَ مِنْ حُسْنِهِ فَإِذَا هُوَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma kashafa al-lithāma ʿan wajhihi ḥattā ẓahara mā khafiya min ḥusnihi fa-idhā huwa ḍawʾu al-makāni
sentences.l: Then he uncovered the face-veil from his face until there appeared what had been hidden of his beauty, and behold, he was Ḍawʾ al-Makān.
sentences.i: Then he drew the veil from his face, and the beauty it had hidden came into view: it was Ḍawʾ al-Makān.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ بِهِ شَرْكَانُ إِلَّا أَنَّهُ خَافَ عَلَيْهِ مِنِ ازْدِحَامِ الْأَقْرَانِ وَانْطِبَاقِ الشُّجْعَانِ وَذَلِكَ لِأَمْرَيْنِ أَحَدُهُمَا صِغَرُ سِنِّهِ وَصِيَانَتُهُ عَنِ الْعَيْنِ وَالثَّانِي أَنَّ بَقَاءَهُ لِلْمَمْلَكَةِ أَعْظَمُ الْجَنَاحَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa bihi sharrukānu illā annahu khāfa ʿalayhi mini izdiḥāmi al-aqrāni wa-inṭibāqi al-shujʿāni wa-dhālika li-amrayni aḥaduhumā ṣigharu sinnihi wa-ṣiyānatuhu ʿani al-ʿayni wa-al-thānī anna baqāʾahu li-al-mamlakati aʿẓamu al-janāḥayni
sentences.l: And Sharrukān rejoiced in him, except that he feared for him from the crowding of the peers and the closing-in of the brave; and that for two matters: one of them the smallness of his age and his being guarded from the eye, and the second that his remaining for the kingdom is the greater of the two wings.
sentences.i: Sharrukān rejoiced to see him, but feared for him in the press of champions and the clash of the brave, and for two reasons: first, his youth, and the need to keep him from the evil eye; second, that his life was the greater of the kingdom's two wings.
sentences.n: “The greater of the two wings”: of the two brothers on whom the kingdom rests, Ḍawʾ al-Makān, the reigning king, is the one it can least afford to lose; the phrase is compressed, and this is the likeliest reading. فرح بـ: “rejoice in”; li-amrayn: li- “for”, of the reason.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا مَلِكُ إِنَّكَ لَقَدْ خَاطَرْتَ بِنَفْسِكَ فَأَلْصِقْ جَوَادَكَ بِجَوَادِي فَإِنِّي لَا آمَنُ عَلَيْكَ مِنَ الْأَعْدَاءِ وَالْمَصْلَحَةُ فِي أَنْ لَاتَخْرُجَ مِنْ تِلْكَ الْعَصَائِبِ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ نَرْمِيَ الْأَعْدَاءَ بِسَهْمِكَ الصَّائِبِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā maliku innaka la-qad khāṭarta bi-nafsika fa-alṣiq jawādaka bi-jawādī fa-innī lā āmanu ʿalayka mina al-aʿdāʾi wa-al-maṣlaḥatu fī an lā takhruja min tilka al-ʿaṣāʾibi li-ajli an narmiya al-aʿdāʾa bi-sahmika al-ṣāʾibi
sentences.l: And he said to him: O king, you indeed have risked your soul; so make your steed cleave to my steed, for I do not feel safe for you from the enemies; and the good counsel is in that you do not go out from those bands, in order that we may shoot the enemies with your arrow, the hitting.
sentences.i: “My king,” he said, “you have put your life at risk. Keep your horse close beside mine, for I do not feel you are safe from the enemy. The wise course is for you not to leave these troops, so that we may strike the enemy with your unerring arrow.”
sentences.n: The print has با ملك and فاصق, misprints for يا ملك (“O king”) and فالصق (“make cleave”), both corrected here. إنك لقد, with both inna and la-qad, doubles the emphasis. خاطر بنفسه: “risk one's life”, bi- marking what is staked. “Your unerring arrow”: the young king is to direct the fight, not throw himself into it.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ إِنِّي أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أُسَاوِيَكَ فِى النِّزَالِ وَلَا أَبْخَلَ بِنَفْسِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ فِي الْقِتَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni innī aradtu an usāwiyaka fī al-nizāli wa-lā abkhala bi-nafsī bayna yadayka fī al-qitāli
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: I wanted that I equal you in the combat, and not be miserly with my soul between your hands in the fighting.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said, “I wanted to match you in combat, and not to spare my own life as I fight before you.”
sentences.n: The print has قتال, a misprint for فقال (“and he said”), corrected here. بخل بـ: “be sparing of”, bi- marking what is withheld.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ انْطَبَقَتْ عَسَاكِرُ الْإِسْلَامِ عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ وَأَحَاطُوا بِهِمْ مِنْ جَمِيعِ الْأَقْطَارِ وَجَاهَدُوهُمْ حَقَّ الْجِهَادِ وَكَسَرُوا شَوْكَةَ الْكُفْرِ وَالْعِنَادِ وَالْفَسَادِ
sentences.tr: thumma inṭabaqat ʿasākiru al-islāmi ʿalā al-kuffāri wa-aḥāṭū bihim min jamīʿi al-aqṭāri wa-jāhadūhum ḥaqqa al-jihādi wa-kasarū shawkata al-kufri wa-al-ʿinādi wa-al-fasādi
sentences.l: Then the armies of Islam closed upon the unbelievers, and surrounded them from all the quarters, and strove against them the true striving, and broke the thorn of unbelief and obstinacy and corruption.
sentences.i: Then the armies of Islam closed in on the unbelievers, surrounded them on every side, fought them as holy war should be fought, and broke the might of unbelief, obstinacy and corruption.
sentences.n: The print has والنساد, a misprint for والفساد (“and corruption”), corrected here. حق الجهاد echoes Qurʾān 22:78. “Thorn” (shawka) is the usual figure for armed might. أحاط بـ: “surround”, the verb takes bi-.

sentences.t: فَتَأَسَّفَ الْمَلِكُ أَفْرِيدُونُ لَمَّا رَأَى مَاحَلَّ بِالرُّومِ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ الْمَذْمُومِ وَقَدْ وَلَّوُا الْأَدْبَارَ وَرَكَنُوا إِلَى الْفِرَارِ يَقْصِدُونَ الْمَرَاكِبَ
sentences.tr: fa-taʾassafa al-maliku afrīdūnu lammā raʾā mā ḥalla bi-al-rūmi mina al-amri al-madhmūmi wa-qad wallawu al-adbāra wa-rakanū ilā al-firāri yaqṣidūna al-marākiba
sentences.l: And King Afrīdūn grieved when he saw what had alighted upon the Rūm of the blameworthy matter, and they had turned the backs and inclined to flight, making for the ships.
sentences.i: King Afrīdūn was grieved to see the disaster that had befallen the Rūm, who had turned their backs and taken to flight, making for the ships.
sentences.n: حلّ بـ: “befall”, bi- marking the one it lands on. The print runs ما and حل together.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِالْعَسَاكِرِ قَدْ خَرَجَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ سَاحِلِ الْبَحْرِ وَفِي أَوَّلِهِمُ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ مُجَنْدِلُ الشُّجْعَانِ وَضَرَبَ فِيهِمْ بِالسَّيْفِ وَالسِّنَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-ʿasākiri qad kharajat ʿalayhim min sāḥili al-baḥri wa-fī awwalihimu al-wazīru dandānu mujandilu al-shujʿāni wa-ḍaraba fīhim bi-al-sayfi wa-al-sināni
sentences.l: And behold, the armies had come out upon them from the shore of the sea, and at their head the vizier Dandān, the thrower-down of the brave, and he struck among them with the sword and the spear-head.
sentences.i: And behold, troops came out at them from the seashore, led by the vizier Dandān, who laid the brave in the dust, and he struck among them with sword and spear.
sentences.n: These are the twenty thousand horsemen hidden by the shore in the night before. Wa-idhā bi-: the bi- only marks what appears.

sentences.t: وَكَذَا الْأَمِيرُ بَهْرَامُ صَاحِبُ دَوَائِرِ الشَّامِ وَهُوَ فِي عِشْرِينَ أَلْفَ ضِرْغَامٍ وَأَحَاطَتْ بِهِمْ عَسَاكِرُ الْإِسْلَامِ مِنْ خَلْفٍ وَمِنْ أَمَامٍ
sentences.tr: wa-kadhā al-amīru bahrāmu ṣāḥibu dawāʾiri al-shāmi wa-huwa fī ʿishrīna alfa ḍirghāmin wa-aḥāṭat bihim ʿasākiru al-islāmi min khalfin wa-min amāmin
sentences.l: And likewise the emir Bahrām, master of the districts of Syria, and he in twenty thousand lions; and the armies of Islam surrounded them from behind and from in front.
sentences.i: So too the emir Bahrām, lord of the districts of Syria, with twenty thousand lion-hearted men; and the armies of Islam hemmed them in from behind and before.
sentences.n: Rhymed: al-shām / ḍirghām / al-islām / amām.

sentences.t: وَمَالَتْ فِرْقَةٌ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ عَلَى مَنْ كَانَ فِى الْمَرَاكِبِ وَأَوْقَعُوا فِيهِمُ الْمَعَاطِبَ فَرَمَوْا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فِي الْبَحْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-mālat firqatun mina al-muslimīna ʿalā man kāna fī al-marākibi wa-awqaʿū fīhimu al-maʿāṭiba fa-ramaw anfusahum fī al-baḥri
sentences.l: And a band of the Muslims turned upon whoever was in the ships, and brought down among them the destructions, so they threw themselves into the sea.
sentences.i: A company of the Muslims fell upon those in the ships and wrought havoc among them, so that they threw themselves into the sea.

sentences.t: وَقَتَلُوا مِنْهُمْ جَمْعًا عَظِيمًا يَزِيدُ عَنْ مِئَةِ أَلْفِ بِطْرِيقٍ وَلَمْ يَنْجُ مِنْ أَبْطَالِهِمْ صَغِيرٌ وَلَاكَبِيرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-qatalū minhum jamʿan ʿaẓīman yazīdu ʿan miʾati alfi biṭrīqin wa-lam yanju min abṭālihim ṣaghīrun wa-lā kabīrun
sentences.l: And they killed of them a great multitude, exceeding a hundred thousand patricians, and there did not escape of their champions small nor great.
sentences.i: They killed a great host of them, more than a hundred thousand patricians, and not one of their champions, small or great, escaped.
sentences.n: Biṭrīq, “patrician”, is used loosely in the tale for any Christian officer or noble. The print runs ولا and كبير together.

sentences.t: وَأَخَذُوا مَرَاكِبَهُمْ بِمَا فِيهَا مِنَ الْأَمْوَالِ وَالذَّخَائِرِ وَالْأَثْقَالِ إِلَّاعِشْرِينَ مَرْكَبًا
sentences.tr: wa-akhadhū marākibahum bi-mā fīhā mina al-amwāli wa-al-dhakhāʾiri wa-al-athqāli illā ʿishrīna markaban
sentences.l: And they took their ships with what was in them of the wealth and the stores and the baggage, except twenty ships.
sentences.i: They took their ships with all the wealth, stores and baggage aboard, all but twenty.
sentences.n: The print runs إلا and عشرين together. Bi-mā fīhā: bi- “with”, the ships together with their contents.

sentences.t: وَغَنِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ فِى ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ غَنِيمَةً مَا غَنِمَ أَحَدٌ مِثْلَهَا فِي سَالِفِ الزَّمَانِ وَلَاسَمِعَتْ أُذُنٌ بِمِثْلِ هَذَا الْحَرْبِ وَالطِّعَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-ghanima al-muslimūna fī dhālika al-yawmi ghanīmatan mā ghanima aḥadun mithlahā fī sālifi al-zamāni wa-lā samiʿat udhunun bi-mithli hādhā al-ḥarbi wa-al-ṭiʿāni
sentences.l: And the Muslims took booty on that day, a booty the like of which no one took in bygone time, nor did an ear hear of the like of this war and lance-thrusting.
sentences.i: That day the Muslims took such spoil as no one had taken in all time past, and no ear had heard of such fighting and spear-play.
sentences.n: هذا الحرب: ḥarb, “war”, is usually feminine; the text makes it masculine. سمع بـ: “hear of”. The print runs ولا and سمعت together.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ جُمْلَةِ مَاغَنِمُوهُ خَمْسُونَ أَلْفًامِنَ الْخَيْلِ غَيْرَ الذَّخَائِرِ وَالْأَسْلَابِ بِمَا لَايُحِيطُ بِهِ حَصْرٌ وَلَاحِسَابٌ
sentences.tr: wa-min jumlati mā ghanimūhu khamsūna alfan mina al-khayli ghayra al-dhakhāʾiri wa-al-aslābi bi-mā lā yuḥīṭu bihi ḥaṣrun wa-lā ḥisābun
sentences.l: And among the sum of what they took as booty, fifty thousand of the horses, besides the stores and the spoils, in what no counting nor reckoning encompasses.
sentences.i: Among the spoil were fifty thousand horses, besides stores and plunder past all counting and reckoning.
sentences.n: The print runs ألفا and من together. بما لا يحيط به: bi- “in (an amount)”, “to a degree that no count can take in”.

sentences.t: وَفَرِحُوا فَرَحًا مَا عَلَيْهِ مَزِيدٌ بِمَا مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ النَّصْرِ وَالتَّأْيِيدِ
sentences.tr: wa-fariḥū faraḥan mā ʿalayhi mazīdun bi-mā manna allāhu ʿalayhim mina al-naṣri wa-al-taʾyīdi
sentences.l: And they rejoiced with a rejoicing above which there is no increase, at what God had bestowed upon them of victory and support.
sentences.i: and they rejoiced beyond measure at the victory and help God had granted them.
sentences.n: Rhymed: mazīd / al-taʾyīd. Bi-mā: bi- “at”, the cause of the joy.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَاكَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْمُنْهَزِمِينَ فَإِنَّهُمْ وَصَلُوا إِلَى الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amrihim wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-munhazimīna fa-innahum waṣalū ilā al-qusṭanṭīniyyati
sentences.l: This is what was of their affair; and as for what was of the affair of the routed, they arrived at Constantinople.
sentences.i: So much for them. As for the routed, they reached Constantinople.
sentences.n: The storyteller's formula for turning from one party to another.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْخَبَرُ قَدْ وَصَلَ إِلَى أَهْلِهَا أَوَّلًا بِأَنَّ الْمَلِكَ أَفْرِيدُونَ هُوَ الظَّافِرُ بِالْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-khabaru qad waṣala ilā ahlihā awwalan bi-anna al-malika afrīdūna huwa al-ẓāfiru bi-al-muslimīna
sentences.l: And the news had reached its people first, that King Afrīdūn was the victor over the Muslims.
sentences.i: The first news to reach its people had been that King Afrīdūn had won the day against the Muslims.
sentences.n: ظفر بـ: “prevail over”, bi- marking the defeated. Bi-anna: bi- “that”, giving the content of the news.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْعَجُوزُ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي أَنَا أَعْلَمُ أَنَّ وَلَدِي مَلِكَ الرُّومِ لَايَكُونُ مِنَ الْمُنْهَزِمِينَ وَلَا يَخَافُ مِنَ الْجُيُوشِ الْإِسْلَامِيَّةِ وَيَرُدُّ أَهْلَ الْأَرْضِ إِلَى الْمِلَّةِ النَّصْرَانِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-ʿajūzu dhātu al-dawāhī anā aʿlamu anna waladī malika al-rūmi lā yakūnu mina al-munhazimīna wa-lā yakhāfu mina al-juyūshi al-islāmiyyati wa-yaruddu ahla al-arḍi ilā al-millati al-naṣrāniyyati
sentences.l: And the old woman, the one of calamities, said: I know that my son, the king of the Rūm, is not of the routed, and does not fear the Islamic armies, and will return the people of the earth to the Christian creed.
sentences.i: The old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī said, “I knew my son the king of the Rūm would not be among the routed, nor afraid of the armies of Islam, and that he will bring the people of the earth back to the Christian faith.”
sentences.n: Dhāt al-Dawāhī, “She of the Calamities”, is the old woman's name in the tale; she is the king of the Rūm's mother. The print runs لا and يكون together.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْعَجُوزَ كَانَتْ أَمَرَتِ الْمَلِكَ الْأَكْبَرَ أَفْرِيدُونَ أَنْ يُزَيِّنَ الْبَلَدَ فَأَظْهَرُوا السُّرُورَ وَشَرِبُوا الْخُمُورَ وَمَاعَلِمُوا بِالْمَقْدُورِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ʿajūza kānat amarati al-malika al-akbara afrīdūna an yuzayyina al-balada fa-aẓharū al-surūra wa-sharibū al-khumūra wa-mā ʿalimū bi-al-maqdūri
sentences.l: Then the old woman had ordered the greater king, Afrīdūn, that he adorn the city; so they showed gladness and drank the wines, and they did not know of what was decreed.
sentences.i: The old woman had told the high king Afrīdūn to deck out the city, so they made merry and drank wine, knowing nothing of what fate had decreed.
sentences.n: Rhymed: al-surūr / al-khumūr / al-maqdūr. علم بـ: “know of”. The print runs ما and علموا together.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ فِي وَسْطِ الْأَفْرَاحِ إِذْ نَعَقَ عَلَيْهِمْ غُرَابُ الْحُزْنِ وَالْأَتْرَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā hum fī wasṭi al-afrāḥi idh naʿaqa ʿalayhim ghurābu al-ḥuzni wa-al-atrāḥi
sentences.l: And while they were in the midst of the rejoicings, lo, there croaked over them the raven of grief and sorrows.
sentences.i: And while they were in the midst of their rejoicing, the raven of grief and sorrow croaked over them.
sentences.n: The raven is the bird of ill omen and of parting.

sentences.t: وَأَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الْعِشْرُونَ مَرْكَبًا الْهَارِبَةُ وَفِيهَا مَلِكُ الرُّومِ
sentences.tr: wa-aqbalat ʿalayhimu al-ʿishrūna markaban al-hāribatu wa-fīhā maliku al-rūmi
sentences.l: And there came toward them the twenty ships, the fleeing, and in them the king of the Rūm.
sentences.i: The twenty ships that had escaped came in, with the king of the Rūm aboard.

sentences.t: فَقَابَلَهُمْ أَفْرِيدُونُ مَلِكُ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ عَلَى السَّاحِلِ وَأَخْبَرُوهُ بِمَا جَرَى لَهُمْ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَزَادَ بُكَاؤُهُمْ وَعَلَا نَحِيبُهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qābalahum afrīdūnu maliku al-qusṭanṭīniyyati ʿalā al-sāḥili wa-akhbarūhu bi-mā jarā lahum mina al-muslimīna fa-zāda bukāʾuhum wa-ʿalā naḥībuhum
sentences.l: And Afrīdūn, king of Constantinople, met them on the shore, and they informed him of what had befallen them from the Muslims; and their weeping increased and their wailing rose.
sentences.i: Afrīdūn, king of Constantinople, met them on the shore, and they told him what the Muslims had done to them; and their weeping grew and their wailing rose.
sentences.n: أخبر بـ: “inform of”, bi- marking the news.

sentences.t: وَانْقَلَبَتْ بِشَارَاتُ الْخَيْرِ بِالْغَمِّ وَالضَّيْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-inqalabat bishārātu al-khayri bi-al-ghammi wa-al-ḍayri
sentences.l: And the glad-tidings of good were turned over into sorrow and harm.
sentences.i: The good tidings were turned to grief and harm.
sentences.n: انقلب بـ: “be turned into”, with bi- marking what it became. Rhymed: al-khayr / al-ḍayr.

sentences.t: وَأَخْبَرُوهُ أَنَّ لُوقَا بْنَ شَمْلُوطَ حَلَّتْ بِهِ النَّوَائِبُ وَتَمَكَّنَ مِنْهُ سَهْمُ الْمَنِيَّةِ الصَّائِبُ
sentences.tr: wa-akhbarūhu anna lūqā bna shamlūṭa ḥallat bihi al-nawāʾibu wa-tamakkana minhu sahmu al-maniyyati al-ṣāʾibu
sentences.l: And they informed him that Lūqā son of Shamlūṭ — the misfortunes had alighted upon him, and the arrow of death, the hitting, had taken hold of him.
sentences.i: They told him that misfortune had overtaken Lūqā son of Shamlūṭ, and death's unerring arrow had struck him home.

sentences.t: فَقَامَتْ عَلَى الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ الْقِيَامَةُ وَعَلِمَ أَنَّ اعْوِجَاجَهُمْ لَيْسَ لَهُ اسْتِقَامَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāmat ʿalā al-maliki afrīdūna al-qiyāmatu wa-ʿalima anna iʿwijājahum laysa lahu istiqāmatun
sentences.l: And the Resurrection rose upon King Afrīdūn, and he knew that their crookedness had no straightening.
sentences.i: It was the Day of Judgement for King Afrīdūn: he knew their ruin could not be set right.
sentences.n: “The Resurrection rose upon him” is the idiom for utter dismay. Rhymed and punning: al-qiyāma / istiqāma, both from the root q-w-m.

sentences.t: وَقَامَتْ بَيْنَهُمُ الْمَآتِمُ وَانْحَلَّتْ مِنْهُمُ الْعَزَائِمُ وَنَدَبَتِ النَّوَادِبُ وَعَلَا النَّحِيبُ وَالْبُكَاءُ مِنْ كُلِّ جَانِبٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qāmat baynahumu al-maʾātimu wa-inḥallat minhumu al-ʿazāʾimu wa-nadabati al-nawādibu wa-ʿalā al-naḥību wa-al-bukāʾu min kulli jānibin
sentences.l: And the mourning-gatherings rose up among them, and the resolves were loosened from them, and the wailing-women keened, and the wailing and the weeping rose from every side.
sentences.i: Mourning was held among them, their resolve gave way, the keening women wailed, and lament and weeping rose on every side.
sentences.n: The print sets المآتم (“mourning-gatherings”) with a sukūn on the lām and a bare alif; the madda is supplied in the pointing.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا دَخَلَ مَلِكُ الرُّومِ عَلَى الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ وَأَخْبَرَهُ بِحَقِيقَةِ الْحَالِ وَأَنَّ هَزِيمَةَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ كَانَتْ عَلَى وَجْهِ الْخِدَاعِ وَالْمِحَالِ قَالَ لَهُ لَا تَنْتَظِرْ أَنْ يَصِلَ مِنَ الْعَسْكَرِ إِلَّا مَنْ وَصَلَ إِلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: wa-lammā dakhala maliku al-rūmi ʿalā al-maliki afrīdūna wa-akhbarahu bi-ḥaqīqati al-ḥāli wa-anna hazīmata al-muslimīna kānat ʿalā wajhi al-khidāʿi wa-al-miḥāli qāla lahu lā tantaẓir an yaṣila mina al-ʿaskari illā man waṣala ilayka
sentences.l: And when the king of the Rūm entered upon King Afrīdūn and informed him of the truth of the state, and that the defeat of the Muslims had been by way of deceit and trickery, he said to him: Do not wait that there arrive of the army except whoever has arrived to you.
sentences.i: When the king of the Rūm came in to King Afrīdūn and told him how things truly stood — that the Muslims' flight had been a feint and a trick — he said to him, “Expect no more of the army to come back than those who have reached you.”
sentences.n: The print has واما (“and as for”) and همزيمة, misprints for ولما (“and when”) and هزيمة (“defeat”), both corrected here. أخبر بـ: “inform of”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْمَلِكُ أَفْرِيدُونُ ذَلِكَ الْكَلَامَ وَقَعَ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ وَصَارَ أَنْفُهُ تَحْتَ قَدَمَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-maliku afrīdūnu dhālika al-kalāma waqaʿa maghshiyyan ʿalayhi wa-ṣāra anfuhu taḥta qadamayhi
sentences.l: And when King Afrīdūn heard that speech, he fell fainted-upon, and his nose came to be beneath his feet.
sentences.i: When King Afrīdūn heard this he fell down in a swoon, his nose beneath his feet.
sentences.n: “His nose beneath his feet”: he collapsed in a heap, an image of utter abasement.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَعَلَّ الْمَسِيحَ غَضِبَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَتَّى أَوْصَلَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ إِلَيْهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla laʿalla al-masīḥa ghaḍiba ʿalayhim ḥattā awṣala al-muslimīna ilayhim
sentences.l: And he said: Perhaps the Messiah was angry with them, so that he brought the Muslims through to them.
sentences.i: Then he said, “The Messiah must have been angry with them, to let the Muslims get at them.”

sentences.t: فَأَقْبَلَ الْبِطْرِيقُ الْكَبِيرُ عَلَى الْمَلِكِ مَهْمُومًا فَقَالَ لَهُ الْمَلِكُ يَا أَبَانَا قَدْ وَقَعَ فِي عَسْكَرِنَا الْفَنَاءُ وَجَزَانَا الْمَسِيحُ
sentences.tr: fa-aqbala al-biṭrīqu al-kabīru ʿalā al-maliki mahmūman fa-qāla lahu al-maliku yā abānā qad waqaʿa fī ʿaskarinā al-fanāʾu wa-jazānā al-masīḥu
sentences.l: And the great patriarch came toward the king, care-laden, and the king said to him: O our father, annihilation has fallen upon our army, and the Messiah has requited us.
sentences.i: The great patriarch came to the king, heavy with care, and the king said to him, “Father, our army has been destroyed; the Messiah has paid us back.”
sentences.n: Biṭrīq, elsewhere a patrician, is here the patriarch, head of the Church; the king calls him “our father”. جزانا: “has paid us out”, for some sin.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْبِطْرِيقُ لَا تَغْتَمُّوا وَلَا تَحْزَنُوا فَإِنَّهُ لَابُدَّأَنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ فَعَلَ ذَنْبًا فِي حَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ وَعُوقِبَ الْجَمِيعُ بِذَنْبِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-biṭrīqu lā taghtammū wa-lā taḥzanū fa-innahu lā budda anna aḥadakum faʿala dhanban fī ḥaqqi al-masīḥi wa-ʿūqiba al-jamīʿu bi-dhanbihi
sentences.l: And the patriarch said: Do not be grieved and do not be sad, for there is no escape but that one of you did a sin against the right of the Messiah, and the whole were punished for his sin.
sentences.i: The patriarch said, “Do not grieve, do not be sad. One of you must have sinned against the Messiah, and all have been punished for that one man's sin.
sentences.n: The print runs لا بد and أن together (لابدان). Bi-dhanbihi: bi- “for”, the cause of the punishment.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنِ الْآنَ نَقْرَأُكُمُ الدُّعَاءَ فِي الْبِيَعِ حَتَّى تَنْدَفِعَ عَنْكُمْ هَذِهِ الْعَسَاكِرُ الْمُحَمَّدِيَّةُ
sentences.tr: wa-lākini al-āna naqraʾukumu al-duʿāʾa fī al-biyaʿi ḥattā tandafiʿa ʿankum hādhihi al-ʿasākiru al-muḥammadiyyatu
sentences.l: But now we recite-you the prayer in the churches, so that these Muḥammadan armies may be driven off from you.
sentences.i: But now we will say the prayers for you in the churches, so that these armies of Muḥammad may be turned away from you.”
sentences.n: نقرأكم, literally “we recite you”, is colloquial for “we recite for you”. Biyaʿ (singular bīʿa) are Christian churches; the print points this word itself.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَتَتِ الْعَجُوزُ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي وَقَالَتْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ إِنَّ عَسْكَرَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ كَثِيرٌ وَنَحْنُ مَا نَصِلُ إِلَيْهِمْ إِلَّا بِالْحِيلَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma baʿda dhālika atati al-ʿajūzu dhātu al-dawāhī wa-qālat ayyuhā al-maliku inna ʿaskara al-muslimīna kathīrun wa-naḥnu mā naṣilu ilayhim illā bi-al-ḥīlati
sentences.l: Then after that the old woman, the one of calamities, came and said: O king, the army of the Muslims is many, and we do not reach to them except by the stratagem.
sentences.i: After that the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī came and said, “O king, the Muslims' army is large; we can only get at them by guile.
sentences.n: Bi-al-ḥīla: bi- “by”, of means.

sentences.t: وَإِنِّي عَوَّلْتُ أَنْ أَعْمَلَ حِيلَةً وَمَكِيدَةً وَأَمْضِيَ إِلَى هَذِهِ الْعَسَاكِرِ الْإِسْلَامِيَّةِ لَعَلِّي أَبْلُغُ غَرَضِي مِنَ الْمُقَدَّمِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَقْتُلُ فَارِسَهُمْ مِثْلَ مَا قَتَلْتُ أَبَاهُ
sentences.tr: wa-innī ʿawwaltu an aʿmala ḥīlatan wa-makīdatan wa-amḍiya ilā hādhihi al-ʿasākiri al-islāmiyyati laʿallī ablughu gharaḍī mina al-muqaddami ʿalayhim wa-aqtulu fārisahum mithla mā qataltu abāhu
sentences.l: And I have resolved that I work a stratagem and a plot and go to these Islamic armies; perhaps I may attain my aim from the one put in command over them, and kill their horseman, like what I killed his father.
sentences.i: I have made up my mind to devise a trick and a snare and go to these armies of Islam; perhaps I can have my will of their commander and kill their champion, as I killed his father.
sentences.n: ʿAwwala, “resolve”, is the tale's usual word for making up one's mind. She killed King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, father of Sharrukān and Ḍawʾ al-Makān, earlier in the tale.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا تَمَّتْ حِيلَتِي عَلَيْهِ فَمَا يَرْجِعُ أَحَدٌ مِنْ عَسَاكِرِهِ إِلَى بِلَادِهِ فَإِنَّهُمْ كُلَّهُمْ أَقْوِيَاءُ بِسَبَبِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā tammat ḥīlatī ʿalayhi fa-mā yarjiʿu aḥadun min ʿasākirihi ilā bilādihi fa-innahum kullahum aqwiyāʾu bi-sababihi
sentences.l: And when my stratagem is completed upon him, then none of his armies will return to his lands, for they, all of them, are strong because of him.
sentences.i: Once my trick has worked on him, not one of his soldiers will go home, for they are all strong only through him.
sentences.n: Bi-sababihi: bi- “by”, “by reason of him”.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنِّي أُرِيدُ مِنَ النَّصَارَى الْقَاطِنِينَ بِالشَّامِ الَّذِي يَخْرُجُونَ لِبَيْعِ بَضَائِعِهِمْ فِي كُلِّ شَهْرٍ وَعَامٍ أَنْ يُسَاعِدُونِي فَإِنَّ بِهِمْ يَتِمُّ غَرَضِي
sentences.tr: wa-lākinnī urīdu mina al-naṣārā al-qāṭinīna bi-al-shāmi alladhī yakhrujūna li-bayʿi baḍāʾiʿihim fī kulli shahrin wa-ʿāmin an yusāʿidūnī fa-inna bihim yatimmu gharaḍī
sentences.l: But I want from the Christians dwelling in Syria, who go out for the selling of their goods in every month and year, that they help me, for by them my aim is completed.
sentences.i: But I want the help of the Christians who live in Syria and go out every month and every year to sell their wares; with them my purpose will be achieved.”
sentences.n: الذي for الذين, the singular relative for a plural, is a common Middle Arabic form. Bi-al-shām: bi- “in”; li-bayʿ: li- “for, in order to”; bihim: bi- “through”, of means.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا الْمَلِكُ بِأَىِّ وَقْتٍ تُرِيدِينَ ذَلِكَ الْأَمْرَ يَكُونُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā al-maliku bi-ayyi waqtin turīdīna dhālika al-amra yakūnu
sentences.l: And the king said to her: At what time do you want that matter — it is?
sentences.i: The king said to her, “When do you want this to happen?”
sentences.n: Colloquial: “that matter, it happens” stands for “that the matter should happen”. Bi-ayyi waqt: bi- “at”, of time.

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَتْ بِأَنْ يُحْضَرَ لَهَا مِئَةُ رَجُلٍ مِنْ نَجْرَانِ الشَّامِ فَأَحْضَرُوهُمْ عِنْدَ الْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-amarat bi-an yuḥḍara lahā miʾatu rajulin min najrāni al-shāmi fa-aḥḍarūhum ʿinda al-maliki
sentences.l: And she commanded that there be brought to her a hundred men of Najrān of Syria, and they brought them to the king.
sentences.i: She ordered that a hundred men of the Syrian Najrān be brought to her, and they were fetched before the king.
sentences.n: أمر بـ: “command”, the verb takes its object with bi-. The tale places these Christians in a Syrian Najrān, not the Najrān of Arabia.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمُ الْمَلِكُ أَمَا تَعْلَمُونَ مَاتَمَّ عَلَى النَّصَارَى مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ قَالُوا نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahumu al-maliku a-mā taʿlamūna mā tamma ʿalā al-naṣārā mina al-muslimīna qālū naʿam
sentences.l: And the king said to them: Do you not know what has been completed upon the Christians from the Muslims? They said: Yes.
sentences.i: The king said to them, “Do you not know what the Muslims have done to the Christians?” “Yes,” they said.
sentences.n: The print runs ما and تم together.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمُ الْمَلِكُ اعْلَمُوا أَنَّ هَذِهِ الْمَرْأَةَ وَهَبَتْ نَفْسَهَا لِلْمَسِيحِ وَالْآنَ عَوَّلَتْ أَنْ تَذْهَبَ بِكُمْ فِي زِيِّ الْمُوَحِّدِينَ لِتَدْبِيرِ حِيلَةٍ يَعُودُ نَفْعُهَا عَلَيْنَا وَتَمْنَعُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ مِنَ الْوُصُولِ إِلَيْنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahumu al-maliku iʿlamū anna hādhihi al-marʾata wahabat nafsahā li-al-masīḥi wa-al-āna ʿawwalat an tadhhaba bikum fī ziyyi al-muwaḥḥidīna li-tadbīri ḥīlatin yaʿūdu nafʿuhā ʿalaynā wa-tamnaʿu al-muslimīna mina al-wuṣūli ilaynā
sentences.l: And the king said to them: Know that this woman has given her soul to the Messiah, and now she has resolved that she go with you in the dress of the professors-of-oneness, for the contriving of a stratagem whose benefit returns upon us and that prevents the Muslims from the arriving to us.
sentences.i: The king said, “Know that this woman has given herself to the Messiah, and has now resolved to take you with her dressed as Muslims, to work a trick that will turn to our benefit and keep the Muslims from reaching us.
sentences.n: “The professors of God's oneness” (al-muwaḥḥidūn) are the Muslims. ذهب بـ: “go with, take along”, bi- marking those taken. Li-al-masīḥ: li- “to”; li-tadbīr: li- “for, in order to”.

sentences.t: فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ وَاهِبُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ لِلْمَسِيحِ وَأَنَا أُعْطِيكُمْ قِنْطَارًا مِنَ الذَّهَبِ فَمَنْ سَلِمَ مِنْكُمْ فَلَهُ الْمَالُ وَمَنْ مَاتَ فَيُجَازِيهِ الْمَسِيحُ
sentences.tr: fa-hal antum wāhibūna anfusakum li-al-masīḥi wa-anā uʿṭīkum qinṭāran mina al-dhahabi fa-man salima minkum fa-lahu al-mālu wa-man māta fa-yujāzīhi al-masīḥu
sentences.l: So are you givers of your souls to the Messiah, and I give you a qinṭār of the gold? Then whoever is safe of you, to him the wealth, and whoever dies, the Messiah will reward him.
sentences.i: Will you give yourselves to the Messiah? I will give you a hundredweight of gold: whoever of you comes through safe shall have the money, and whoever dies, the Messiah will reward him.”
sentences.n: A qinṭār is a great weight, roughly a hundredweight. Fa-lahu: li- “to”, the money is his.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ قَدْ وَهَبْنَا أَنْفُسَنَا لِلْمَسِيحِ وَنَحْنُ فِدَاؤُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū ayyuhā al-maliku qad wahabnā anfusanā li-al-masīḥi wa-naḥnu fidāʾuka
sentences.l: And they said: O king, we have given our souls to the Messiah, and we are your ransom.
sentences.i: They said, “O king, we have given ourselves to the Messiah, and we would lay down our lives for you.”

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَخَذَتِ الْعَجُوزُ جَمِيعَ مَا تَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ مِنَ الْعَقَاقِيرِ وَوَضَعَتْهُمْ فِى الْمَاءِ وَغَلَتْهُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ فَانْحَلَّ السَّوَادُ وَصَبَرَتْ حَتَّى بَرَدَتْ فَأَرْخَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ طَرَفَ مِنْدِيلٍ طَوِيلٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika akhadhati al-ʿajūzu jamīʿa mā taḥtāju ilayhi mina al-ʿaqāqīri wa-waḍaʿathum fī al-māʾi wa-ghalathum ʿalā al-nāri fa-inḥalla al-sawādu wa-ṣabarat ḥattā baradat fa-arkhat ʿalayhim ṭarafa mindīlin ṭawīlin
sentences.l: And at that the old woman took all that she needed of the drugs, and put them in the water, and boiled them on the fire, and the blackness dissolved; and she waited until it cooled, and let down over them the end of a long kerchief.
sentences.i: Then the old woman took all the drugs she needed, put them in water and boiled them over the fire, and the blackness dissolved. She waited until it had cooled, and let the end of a long kerchief hang down over them.
sentences.n: The print says no more than this, and what she does with the brew is left unclear; “them” may be the drugs. The masculine plural pronouns for the drugs (wa-waḍaʿathum, ghalathum, ʿalayhim) are colloquial, and ghalā, “boil”, is used as a transitive verb.

sentences.t: وَلَبِسَتْ فَوْقَ أَثْوَابِهَا مُلُوطَةً مُطَرَّزَةً بِطِرَازٍ وَبِيَدِهَا تَسْبِيحٌ
sentences.tr: wa-labisat fawqa athwābihā mulūṭatan muṭarrazatan bi-ṭirāzin wa-bi-yadihā tasbīḥun
sentences.l: And she put on above her clothes a mulūṭa embroidered with an embroidered-band, and in her hand a rosary.
sentences.i: Over her clothes she put on a cloak worked with an embroidered band, and in her hand she held a rosary.
sentences.n: A mulūṭa is a cloak or loose outer gown. Tasbīḥ, properly “glorifying God”, stands here for the prayer-beads on which the praises are counted. Bi-ṭirāz: bi- “with”; bi-yadihā: bi- “in”.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ دَخَلَتْ عَلَى الْمَلِكِ فَلَمْ يَعْرِفْهَا وَلَا أَحَدٌ مِنَ الْجَالِسِينَ فَكَشَفَتْ لَهُمْ مِنْ وَجْهِهَا فَمَا فِى الْمَجْلِسِ أَحَدٌ إِلَّاشَكَرَهَا عَلَى مَكْرِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika dakhalat ʿalā al-maliki fa-lam yaʿrifhā wa-lā aḥadun mina al-jālisīna fa-kashafat lahum min wajhihā fa-mā fī al-majlisi aḥadun illā shakarahā ʿalā makrihā
sentences.l: And after that she entered upon the king, and he did not know her, nor anyone of those sitting; and she uncovered for them (some) of her face, and there was not in the assembly anyone but thanked her for her cunning.
sentences.i: Then she went in to the king, and neither he nor any of those sitting with him knew her, until she uncovered part of her face to them; and there was no one in the assembly who did not praise her for her cunning.
sentences.n: The print runs إلا and شكرها together.

sentences.t: وَفَرِحَ ابْنُهَا وَقَالَ لَاعَدِمَ الْمَسِيحُ طَلْعَتَكِ
sentences.tr: wa-fariḥa ibnuhā wa-qāla lā ʿadima al-masīḥu ṭalʿataki
sentences.l: And her son rejoiced, and said: May the Messiah not lack your countenance!
sentences.i: Her son was delighted and said, “May the Messiah never be without the sight of your face!”
sentences.n: Her son is the king of the Rūm. A blessing on the pattern of lā ʿadimnāki, “may we never lose you”; the pointing is one reading of a compressed formula, which the print runs together (لاعدم).

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ خَرَجَتْ وَمَعَهَا النَّصَارَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ نَجْرَانِ الشَّامِ وَسَارُوا طَالِبِينَ عَسْكَرَ بَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika kharajat wa-maʿahā al-naṣārā alladhīna min najrāni al-shāmi wa-sārū ṭālibīna ʿaskara baghdāda
sentences.l: And at that she went out, and with her the Christians who were from Najrān of Syria, and they journeyed, seeking the army of Baghdad.
sentences.i: Then she set out with the Christians of the Syrian Najrān, and they journeyed on, making for the army of Baghdad.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula, as in every night. The print has المباج, a misprint for المباح (“permitted”), corrected here.
